findings.issue_text: [BUG] The `queued` field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value carries the process-start timestamp, not the enqueue time. Every cross-system assignment records the worker process's import time as its queue timestamp; ordering/diagnostic data is silently wrong for all consumers of `queued`, and the value never updates no matter when the object is built.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `asdict`) emits a raw `datetime` for `queued`, which is placed into Celery `apply_async` kwargs that must be JSON-serializable. With the standard JSON task serializer, enqueueing `sync_assignee_outbound` with an assignment source raises EncodeError (Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable) at apply_async time, so the assignee sync is never queued and the outbound assignment silently never happens whenever the source is set.

[BUG] The task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` but the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` on IssueSyncIntegration (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py ~line 400) was not updated to accept the new keyword, and none of the existing provider implementations (Jira, VSTS, etc.) in this diff were updated either. Any integration whose `sync_assignee_outbound` implementation does not already declare `**kwargs` (or the new parameter) raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source' inside the Celery task whenever an assignment_source is present, killing the assignee sync for that provider.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` reconstructs via `cls(**input_dict)` without validating or coercing the `queued` value, so a round-tripped dict (where the datetime has become an ISO string under JSON) produces an AssignmentSource whose `queued` field is a `str` rather than a `datetime`. Any consumer that later treats `assignment_source.queued` as a datetime (comparison, formatting, storage) crashes or misbehaves; the type annotation on the dataclass field is a lie after deserialization, so the defect surfaces far from its cause.

[BUG] assignment_source_dict passed through apply_async kwargs contains a raw datetime (the 'queued' field from AssignmentSource.to_dict), which the Celery JSON serializer cannot encode. sync_group_assignee_outbound in sync.py builds kwargs with assignment_source.to_dict() where to_dict() = asdict(self) and self.queued is a datetime; apply_async with the default JSON serializer raises TypeError('Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable'), so the assignee sync task is never enqueued and outbound assignee sync silently stops working whenever an inbound integration assignment occurs — exactly the new feature's main path.

[BUG] The `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` dataclass field default is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance created in the process shares a single stale timestamp. All AssignmentSource objects report the process start time as their 'queued' time; any consumer using that field to detect stale/duplicate syncs or record propagation latency gets wrong data for every instance created after the first import.

[ADVISORY] The cycle-prevention mechanism is only wired into the assignee sync path: the abstract sync_status_outbound gained an assignment_source parameter that no caller in the diff ever passes, and the inbound status path (sync_status_inbound_task) never creates or propagates an AssignmentSource. Status sync cycles (inbound status resolution triggering outbound status sync back to the source integration) remain unprevented even though should_sync's new check and the sync_status_outbound signature suggest the feature covers status; the new parameter on sync_status_outbound is dead code that every subclass must now carry without benefit, and users of bidirectional status sync will still see infinite ping-pong resolution loops.

[ADVISORY] The core new behavior — that an assignment sourced from a DIFFERENT integration still propagates outward — has no test; only the same-integration suppression is exercised, so the comment's claimed property 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' is unverified. A regression that over-blocks (e.g., a future change comparing provider names instead of integration_id, or an exception path in should_sync returning False) would silently kill all cross-integration assignee propagation, and the existing test suite would stay green because only the negative case is asserted.

[ADVISORY] The new assignment_source_dict kwarg creates rolling-deploy skew: sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async now always includes the key, but pre-deploy workers define sync_assignee_outbound without that parameter. During a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new code are consumed by old workers, which raise TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict' — inbound-driven assignee syncs fail and the tasks are lost (retried into the same error) until every worker is upgraded.

[ADVISORY] No test covers from_dict with a 'queued' value coming back from the queue (round-trip through to_dict), the path actually exercised by the Celery task, so the datetime-in-payload failure mode is untested. If/when the serialization bug in the task kwarg is hit or fixed, no test asserts the round-trip contract (to_dict → from_dict) that the task relies on; a fix like ISO-formatting the datetime changes the payload shape and from_dict's datetime parsing has zero coverage, so the task would silently receive queued as a string and crash on comparison or persist wrong data.

[ADVISORY] The `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` field is a dataclass default evaluated once at import time, and it is never read anywhere in the diff — it is not traceable to the stated cycle-prevention requirement. Every AssignmentSource carries a meaningless import-time timestamp, and the field creates a latent serialization bug: `to_dict()` emits a raw datetime into Celery `apply_async` kwargs, which the default JSON task serializer rejects, so every outbound assignee sync that carries a source fails at enqueue and cycle protection silently never engages in production. The field should be deleted (or computed per-instance in `from_integration`) since nothing consumes it.

[ADVISORY] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller in the diff passes and no shown implementation uses — dead public-surface expansion. Every concrete integration subclass must now accept a parameter that is never exercised, and out-of-tree/monorepo implementations that don't add the kwarg are fine only because nothing passes it; the next caller that does pass it will TypeError against un-updated implementations. This parameter is not traceable to any requirement in the diff and should be removed until status-sync cycle prevention is actually implemented.

[BUG] Cycle prevention is only wired through the assignee path while the PR claims broad cross-system issue synchronization — status sync (`sync_status_inbound`, `sync_status_outbound` callers) is left untouched, so resolve/unresolve ping-pong cycles are unguarded. An external tool resolving a linked issue triggers `sync_status_inbound` (unchanged), which resolves the Sentry group; if the same integration also has `sync_status_outbound` enabled, the outbound status task fires back to the originating tool — the exact sync-cycle class of bug this PR purports to fix, reproduced for status instead of assignee. This is under-scoping relative to the stated intent, not merely incomplete requirements.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None, which converts any deserialization failure (including the datetime round-trip failure of `queued`) into silent loss of cycle protection rather than an error. A malformed or Celery-JSON-normalized payload (e.g., `queued` arriving as an ISO string) makes `from_dict` return None, `should_sync` then treats the assignment as user-originated, and the outbound sync loops back to the source integration — the invariant the diff exists to enforce is silently violated with no log line to detect it. The `queued` field should be deleted so `from_dict` cannot fail on the datetime, and a failure here should log.

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated exactly once at import time, so every AssignmentSource ever created reports the same (import-time) timestamp as its queue time. Any consumer relying on `queued` to detect stale/replayed sync tasks (e.g. deciding whether an assignment echo is too old to propagate) reads a meaningless constant; the field is derivable data with no valid provenance, and the unit/provenance of the value is silently wrong from day one.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a raw `datetime` (the `queued` field) into the `apply_async` kwargs, a value crossing the queue boundary that the JSON task serializer cannot encode, so the enqueue raises EncodeError instead of queuing the sync task. Every inbound assignee sync that fans out to external issues fails at enqueue time with a serialization error (when the broker enforces JSON), so external assignee updates are never delivered — the sync loop this PR exists to build silently produces no outbound calls while local Sentry assignment still succeeds, making the failure hard to notice.

[BUG] `from_dict` swallows all ValueError/TypeError and returns None, so a partially-corrupted or schema-drifted payload (e.g. an old queued task or a missing/extra key after a future field change) is silently reinterpreted as 'no assignment source'. The cycle-pretection guard in should_sync is keyed entirely on this parsed value; a None return disables loop prevention exactly when the data was present-but-unparseable, reintroducing the ping-pong assign sync loop between Sentry and the external system that this diff was written to prevent — and nothing logs, so operators can't see why suppression stopped working.

[ADVISORY] The sync-cycle suppression compares only `integration_id`, but the same external issue can be linked to multiple GroupLinks/organizations, and status sync (sync_status_inbound/sync_status_outbound) is left with no source tracking at all, so the loop-pretection design only covers the assignee path and one hop. A status round-trip (external resolve -> Sentry resolve -> outbound status sync back to the origin integration) still loops, and any multi-integration topology where integration A's outbound change is credited as a fresh user edit re-enters the cycle; the next change has to thread assignment_source through every sync entry point (status, comments) by hand because the guard is per-method rather than a shared sync-context.

[ADVISORY] `source_name` is stored as a free-form string copied from `integration.name` but never compared or used, making it redundant derived data duplicating `integration_id` with no consumer and no single source of truth (integration names are mutable and will drift from the recorded snapshot). Any future code that dispatches or logs on `source_name` reads a stale copy of a value the integration table owns and may have renamed since; it also bloats every queued task payload for no behavioral gain, and deleting it now costs nothing while it only exists on new call sites.

[BUG] The `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` dataclass default is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` value — including both call sites in sync.py's `from_integration` — carries the server-startup timestamp instead of the time the assignment was actually made. The `queued` timestamp that to_dict() ships into task payloads reflects process start time, not assignment time; anyone debugging sync ordering or cycle detection by that timestamp gets garbage data, and all instances created by a worker share one identical timestamp.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` produces `{'source_name': str, 'integration_id': int, 'queued': datetime}` and this dict is passed directly as Celery task kwargs in `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)`, but a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable by Celery's default JSON serializer. Any inbound assignment that triggers `sync_group_assignee_outbound` with a non-None assignment_source raises a serialization error inside apply_async, so the outbound sync task is never enqueued and the assignee change is silently never propagated to the external issue — the opposite of the PR's cross-system sync intent.

[ADVISORY] The task signature gains a new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg while `sync_group_assignee_outbound` in sync.py immediately starts sending it unconditionally, so during a rolling deploy old workers running the prior `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` signature receive the extra kwarg and raise TypeError. In mixed-version deployments every queued sync_assignee_outbound task that carries an assignment source fails on old workers with an unexpected-keyword-arg TypeError, losing assignee syncs (and their analytics events) until the deploy completes.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows malformed input by returning None, and the task then calls `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)`, which skips the cycle-prevention check entirely because the `sync_source and ...` guard treats None as 'no source'. A payload that fails to reconstruct (e.g., a `queued` value that becomes a non-datetime after crossing a serialization boundary, or extra keys from a future schema) silently disables cycle prevention for that sync, reintroducing the very sync loops this PR was written to prevent — with no log line recording the drop.

[ADVISORY] The cycle-prevention intent is only implemented for assignee sync: `sync_group_assignee_inbound` stamps `assignment_source` on assign/deassign, but `sync_status_inbound` and comment-sync inbound paths were not given the equivalent source tracking, so the stated objective 'prevent sync-cycles' is only partially delivered in this diff. Organizations with two-way status sync enabled still get status ping-pong loops (resolve in Jira -> resolve in Sentry -> re-resolve in Jira), and operators who accepted this PR believing cycle prevention was added will find the assignee-only coverage surprising when the loop they actually hit is a status loop.

[ADVISORY] sync_group_assignee_outbound puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs via AssignmentSource.to_dict(), which a JSON broker serializes to a string and which old workers (pre-deploy) reject as an unexpected kwarg, causing silent task failure during a rolling deploy. During a rolling deploy, new web nodes enqueue sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source_dict while old workers running the 3-arg signature raise TypeError on the unexpected kwarg; the outbound assignee sync is silently dropped (no retry, no error surfaced), so assignees on external issues fall out of sync. Additionally, after JSON round-trip the 'queued' field is a str, not datetime, so any consumer comparing timestamps gets inconsistent types.

[ADVISORY] The new cycle-prevention test (test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration) has no positive control: it only asserts mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called() and never tests the complementary case where assignment_source.integration_id differs from the target integration, which is the branch the code comment explicitly promises to preserve ('This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward', issues.py:388-390). The assert_not_called assertion cannot distinguish the new sync-cycle gate from any pre-existing early return in should_sync (org_integration None, missing key, config False), and the allow-other-integrations branch of the new gate (sync_source set, integration_id different) ships with zero coverage — a regression that flips it to block all outbound syncs whenever sync_source is present would pass this test suite unchanged.

[ADVISORY] The inbound assignment path — sync_group_assignee_inbound now constructing AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration) and threading it into GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign — is exercised by no assertion anywhere in this diff (I checked tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py and tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py, the only test files touched; neither asserts that an inbound sync passes a non-None assignment_source into assign/deassign). The end-to-end cycle-prevention flow the PR exists for (inbound assign from integration A must not bounce back to A but must propagate to linked integration B) is never verified: if from_integration returns a source whose integration_id never matches (e.g. a type mismatch comparing RpcIntegration.id vs int), cycle prevention silently fails in production while all updated tests still pass, because they only cover the None-source path and the directly-injected source path.

[BUG] test_to_dict's assertion `assert result.get("queued") is not None` is a false-confidence assertion that passes regardless of what queued contains, hiding the import-time-default defect in AssignmentSource itself (assignment_source.py:18: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition time, so every instance shares the module-import timestamp). The test never asserts queued's type or that it approximates the current time, so the stale shared default — which makes every AssignmentSource report the server-start time as its queue time — passes CI while making the field semantically wrong for any consumer using it to measure queue latency or staleness.

[ADVISORY] No test covers the to_dict/from_dict round-trip across the task boundary: to_dict emits queued as a datetime object into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs (sync.py:139-144), and from_dict (which is the only rehydration path) is only tested with dicts that omit queued entirely, never with a serialized (string) or datetime-typed queued value. If the broker serializes kwargs as JSON, the datetime either fails to serialize or arrives as a string that makes cls(**input_dict) raise TypeError inside from_dict, which swallows it and returns None — silently disabling cycle prevention for every cross-process sync; if it uses pickle, the round-trip works but is never proven by any test in this diff, so a serializer change breaks the feature with no test failure.

[BUG] The `queued` field is a raw datetime that flows through `to_dict()`/`asdict()` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`, a payload crossing the Celery task-queue boundary that the default JSON serializer cannot encode. As soon as any inbound sync assigns an assignee (sync.py building `assignment_source_dict` via `assignment_source.to_dict()`), `apply_async` raises EncodeError/Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable, so outbound assignee sync tasks are never enqueued and assignee changes silently stop propagating to external issues.

[BUG] The task signature gains a new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg, but during a rolling deploy new producers enqueue tasks with that kwarg while old workers run the previous signature `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)`. Old-version workers consuming the new task payload raise TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict' and the task permanently fails (or retries into failure), so assignee sync events sent during the deploy window are lost for every linked external issue.

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, so it is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time and shared by every instance, not the per-instance enqueue time. Every AssignmentSource created by a long-running worker process reports the process's startup timestamp as its `queued` time; any consumer using `queued` for latency measurement, TTL, or audit of when the assignment originated gets a silently wrong timestamp by hours or days, and this is undetectable in tests that construct the object fresh.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` accepts any keys that match the dataclass fields without type-checking or conversion, so a `queued` value that round-tripped through JSON (an ISO string) is silently accepted as a str rather than a datetime. Once the datetime-serialization issue is 'fixed' by stringifying, every reconstructed AssignmentSource carries `queued` as a string, so any future code that does datetime arithmetic or comparison on `queued` (e.g. cycle-window expiry) crashes or silently miscompares; the round-trip contract between to_dict and from_dict is not lossless and nothing in the diff enforces it.

[BUG] The `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` dataclass default is evaluated exactly once at import time, so every AssignmentSource carries the process-start timestamp instead of the enqueue time. Any staleness/latency logic or debugging based on `queued` reads a timestamp from whenever the worker/monolith process was last deployed or restarted, not when the assignment was actually queued — the field is silently always wrong.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a raw `datetime` (`queued`) into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`, which the JSON task serializer cannot encode. When the assignment originates from an integration (inbound sync path via `sync_group_assignee_inbound`), enqueueing fails with a serialization TypeError raised inside `sync_group_assignee_outbound` during `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, so the inbound webhook that triggered the assign errors out after the local DB assignment is already committed — partial success with no retry of the outbound propagation.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` returns None on any parse failure (wrong/missing keys) and the caller treats None as 'no assignment source', silently disabling the sync-cycle guard. A malformed or version-skewed dict (e.g., a worker running older/newer code, or a string-typed `queued` after JSON round-trip) makes `should_sync` skip the integration_id comparison entirely, so sync cycles the guard was built to prevent resume with no log, metric, or error surfaced anywhere.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` performs no type validation, so a `queued` value that round-tripped through a JSON serializer as an ISO string is accepted and the 'frozen' dataclass silently holds a `str` where the field is declared `datetime`. The next serialization or datetime arithmetic on `queued` (in a worker that did deserialize successfully under a serializer that handles datetimes) hits `TypeError: descriptor 'isoformat' for 'datetime.datetime' objects doesn't apply`-style failures downstream, or produces a mismatched repr in logs, misdirecting debugging of assignment-source staleness.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly wires `AssignmentSource` only through the assignee path: `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` passes `assignment_source` into `GroupAssignee.assign/deassign()`, which passes it to `sync_group_assignee_outbound()`, which serializes it into `sync_assignee_outbound()`, which then calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and forwards `assignment_source` to `sync_assignee_outbound()`. By contrast, although `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` now accepts `sync_source` and `sync_status_outbound()`’s abstract signature now includes `assignment_source`, no status-related caller in this diff passes an `AssignmentSource` into `should_sync` for status attributes, and nothing updates/imports `sync_status_inbound_task` to create/propagate an assignment source. So the finding that the status plumbing is currently unused/incomplete (and forces subclasses to carry a new parameter without demonstrated benefit in this PR) is grounded in the diff. However, the claim about “infinite ping-pong resolution loops” is not directly verifiable from the diff alone, so this is better classified as an incomplete-scope/architecture concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The core new behavior — that an assignment sourced from a DIFFERENT integration still propagates outward — has no test; only the same-integration suppression is exercised, so the comment's claimed property 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' is unverified. A regression that over-blocks (e.g., a future change comparing provider names instead of integration_id, or an exception path in should_sync returning False) would silently kill all cross-integration assignee propagation, and the existing test suite would stay green because only the negative case is asserted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new gating logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to suppress outbound syncing only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, with a comment claiming other integrations should still propagate changes. The new test in `test_groupassignee.py` only asserts the negative case (matching-source integration suppresses outbound) and existing tests cover the `assignment_source=None` path, but there is no test exercising the positive case where `assignment_source` is present and refers to a *different* integration (should still call `sync_assignee_outbound`). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for nontrivial new logic rather than a current functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new assignment_source_dict kwarg creates rolling-deploy skew: sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async now always includes the key, but pre-deploy workers define sync_assignee_outbound without that parameter. During a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new code are consumed by old workers, which raise TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict' — inbound-driven assignee syncs fail and the tasks are lost (retried into the same error) until every worker is upgraded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task signature in `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py` from `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` to include a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict: dict[str, Any] | None = None`. At the same time, `sync_group_assignee_outbound` in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py` now enqueues the task with `apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": ...})`, always including that key (even when the value is `None`). In a rolling deploy, old workers still running the previous task signature would raise `TypeError` on the unexpected kwarg, causing enqueued tasks to fail until all workers are updated. This is a concrete, diff-grounded compatibility issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test covers from_dict with a 'queued' value coming back from the queue (round-trip through to_dict), the path actually exercised by the Celery task, so the datetime-in-payload failure mode is untested. If/when the serialization bug in the task kwarg is hit or fixed, no test asserts the round-trip contract (to_dict → from_dict) that the task relies on; a fix like ISO-formatting the datetime changes the payload shape and from_dict's datetime parsing has zero coverage, so the task would silently receive queued as a string and crash on comparison or persist wrong data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (via `asdict`) which includes a `queued: datetime` field, and passes that dict through Celery kwargs (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` → `sync_assignee_outbound`), where it is parsed with `AssignmentSource.from_dict()`. The new tests only cover `from_dict` with `{}` / invalid keys / valid data *without* `queued`, and `to_dict` only asserts `queued` exists, not that `to_dict() → from_dict()` preserves types/shape. Also, `from_dict` does no datetime parsing/validation (it will accept a string `queued` silently), so a serialization change would be untested. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-coverage issue rather than a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` field is a dataclass default evaluated once at import time, and it is never read anywhere in the diff — it is not traceable to the stated cycle-prevention requirement. Every AssignmentSource carries a meaningless import-time timestamp, and the field creates a latent serialization bug: `to_dict()` emits a raw datetime into Celery `apply_async` kwargs, which the default JSON task serializer rejects, so every outbound assignee sync that carries a source fails at enqueue and cycle protection silently never engages in production. The field should be deleted (or computed per-instance in `from_integration`) since nothing consumes it.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a default evaluated at import time (not per-instance), so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. Additionally, `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which includes this raw `datetime`, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`, meaning Celery task kwargs will contain a `datetime` object. Whether or not the runtime serializer is JSON isn’t shown in the diff, but the diff does verifiably enqueue a non-primitive type in task kwargs, which is a real correctness risk. The cycle-prevention logic only uses `integration_id`, so `queued` is currently unused in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller in the diff passes and no shown implementation uses — dead public-surface expansion. Every concrete integration subclass must now accept a parameter that is never exercised, and out-of-tree/monorepo implementations that don't add the kwarg are fine only because nothing passes it; the next caller that does pass it will TypeError against un-updated implementations. This parameter is not traceable to any requirement in the diff and should be removed until status-sync cycle prevention is actually implemented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff expands the abstract `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound(...)` signature to include `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py) but the diff shows no call sites passing it and no logic consuming it. This is a public-surface/API expansion for all concrete integrations with no demonstrated need in the diff, and it increases maintenance burden / future compatibility risk (a future caller could pass the kwarg and break un-updated overrides). It’s not a verifiable runtime bug from this diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Cycle prevention is only wired through the assignee path while the PR claims broad cross-system issue synchronization — status sync (`sync_status_inbound`, `sync_status_outbound` callers) is left untouched, so resolve/unresolve ping-pong cycles are unguarded. An external tool resolving a linked issue triggers `sync_status_inbound` (unchanged), which resolves the Sentry group; if the same integration also has `sync_status_outbound` enabled, the outbound status task fires back to the originating tool — the exact sync-cycle class of bug this PR purports to fix, reproduced for status instead of assignee. This is under-scoping relative to the stated intent, not merely incomplete requirements.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires `AssignmentSource` through the assignee outbound path (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> task `sync_assignee_outbound` -> `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`), and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` now prevents syncing when `sync_source.integration_id` matches `self.org_integration.integration_id`. However, no analogous plumbing is shown for status sync: while the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature is extended to accept `assignment_source`, the diff does not update any status inbound/outbound callers/tasks to pass an `AssignmentSource` into `should_sync` or into `sync_status_outbound`. So cycle-prevention is demonstrably implemented only for assignee in this change; for status it remains unguarded (at least in this diff). This is a scope/coverage concern rather than a newly introduced functional regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None, which converts any deserialization failure (including the datetime round-trip failure of `queued`) into silent loss of cycle protection rather than an error. A malformed or Celery-JSON-normalized payload (e.g., `queued` arriving as an ISO string) makes `from_dict` return None, `should_sync` then treats the assignment as user-originated, and the outbound sync loops back to the source integration — the invariant the diff exists to enforce is silently violated with no log line to detect it. The `queued` field should be deleted so `from_dict` cannot fail on the datetime, and a failure here should log.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s central claim—`queued` “arriving as an ISO string” causing `AssignmentSource.from_dict` to raise and return `None`, thereby disabling cycle protection—is not supported by the diff. `from_dict` simply does `cls(**input_dict)`, and Python dataclasses do not enforce type annotations at runtime, so a string value for `queued` would not trigger `TypeError`/`ValueError`; it would produce an `AssignmentSource` instance with `queued` as a string, and `should_sync(...)` would still block cycles based on `integration_id`. While swallowing exceptions could hide malformed payloads (missing/extra keys), the specific datetime round-trip failure scenario described is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated exactly once at import time, so every AssignmentSource ever created reports the same (import-time) timestamp as its queue time. Any consumer relying on `queued` to detect stale/replayed sync tasks (e.g. deciding whether an assignment echo is too old to propagate) reads a meaningless constant; the field is derivable data with no valid provenance, and the unit/provenance of the value is silently wrong from day one.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field is declared `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so all `AssignmentSource` instances created without explicitly passing `queued` will share the same timestamp. This is a real correctness bug; it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to capture creation time per instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a raw `datetime` (the `queued` field) into the `apply_async` kwargs, a value crossing the queue boundary that the JSON task serializer cannot encode, so the enqueue raises EncodeError instead of queuing the sync task. Every inbound assignee sync that fans out to external issues fails at enqueue time with a serialization error (when the broker enforces JSON), so external assignee updates are never delivered — the sync loop this PR exists to build silently produces no outbound calls while local Sentry assignment still succeeds, making the failure hard to notice.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does pass `assignment_source.to_dict()` into `apply_async` kwargs (see `sync_group_assignee_outbound`), and `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which includes the `queued` field as a `datetime` object (from `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`). That means a non-primitive value crosses the task-queue boundary. However, the finding’s claim that this *definitely* raises `EncodeError` with the JSON serializer is not verifiable from the diff alone (Celery/Kombu JSON serialization may support datetimes, depending on configuration). Still, embedding a raw `datetime` in task kwargs is a concrete, diff-grounded risk/compatibility issue and should be normalized (e.g., ISO string) or omitted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `from_dict` swallows all ValueError/TypeError and returns None, so a partially-corrupted or schema-drifted payload (e.g. an old queued task or a missing/extra key after a future field change) is silently reinterpreted as 'no assignment source'. The cycle-pretection guard in should_sync is keyed entirely on this parsed value; a None return disables loop prevention exactly when the data was present-but-unparseable, reintroducing the ping-pong assign sync loop between Sentry and the external system that this diff was written to prevent — and nothing logs, so operators can't see why suppression stopped working.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` catching `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returning `None` on any parse problem, and `sync_assignee_outbound` uses that parsed value to decide whether `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` applies the new cycle-prevention guard (which only runs when `sync_source` is truthy). So if `assignment_source_dict` is present but unparseable (extra/missing keys), loop prevention would be skipped and there is no logging. However, the diff itself only produces `assignment_source_dict` via `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` in the same codebase, so under normal operation in this version it will be parseable; the problematic scenario depends on corrupted/stale/future-schema payloads, which is a robustness concern but not a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-cycle suppression compares only `integration_id`, but the same external issue can be linked to multiple GroupLinks/organizations, and status sync (sync_status_inbound/sync_status_outbound) is left with no source tracking at all, so the loop-pretection design only covers the assignee path and one hop. A status round-trip (external resolve -> Sentry resolve -> outbound status sync back to the origin integration) still loops, and any multi-integration topology where integration A's outbound change is credited as a fresh user edit re-enters the cycle; the next change has to thread assignment_source through every sync entry point (status, comments) by hand because the guard is per-method rather than a shared sync-context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AssignmentSource` and a suppression guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)`, but only the assignee outbound path actually threads this through: `sync_group_assignee_outbound(... assignment_source ...)` -> celery `sync_assignee_outbound(... assignment_source_dict ...)` -> `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. While `sync_status_outbound`’s abstract signature is expanded to accept `assignment_source`, there are no corresponding call-site changes in this diff to pass a source into `should_sync("outbound_status"/"outbound_status")` or to otherwise apply the same loop-prevention to status/comments. So the review concern that the loop-prevention is currently scoped to the assignee path and requires manual propagation per entry point is diff-grounded. Claims about multi-organization/multi-GroupLink topologies and an actual status loop occurring aren’t directly verifiable from the shown changes, so this is best treated as an incompleteness/architecture issue rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `source_name` is stored as a free-form string copied from `integration.name` but never compared or used, making it redundant derived data duplicating `integration_id` with no consumer and no single source of truth (integration names are mutable and will drift from the recorded snapshot). Any future code that dispatches or logs on `source_name` reads a stale copy of a value the integration table owns and may have renamed since; it also bloats every queued task payload for no behavioral gain, and deleting it now costs nothing while it only exists on new call sites.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `AssignmentSource` stores both `integration_id` and `source_name` (copied from `integration.name`) and serializes both into task payloads via `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> celery kwargs `assignment_source_dict`, parsed in `sync_assignee_outbound`). However, all new behavioral logic only uses `integration_id` (cycle-prevention in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`: `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`). There is no consumer of `source_name` anywhere in the shown changes, so it is currently redundant derived data that can drift if the integration name changes and marginally bloats queued task payloads. This is a concrete, diff-grounded design/scope concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` dataclass default is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` value — including both call sites in sync.py's `from_integration` — carries the server-startup timestamp instead of the time the assignment was actually made. The `queued` timestamp that to_dict() ships into task payloads reflects process start time, not assignment time; anyone debugging sync ordering or cycle detection by that timestamp gets garbage data, and all instances created by a worker share one identical timestamp.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. That calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so every `AssignmentSource(...)` created without an explicit `queued` value will share the same timestamp (process start). Since `from_integration()` constructs `AssignmentSource` without passing `queued`, and `to_dict()` serializes it into task payloads (`assignment_source.to_dict()` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`), the queued timestamp will be incorrect as described. This should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` produces `{'source_name': str, 'integration_id': int, 'queued': datetime}` and this dict is passed directly as Celery task kwargs in `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)`, but a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable by Celery's default JSON serializer. Any inbound assignment that triggers `sync_group_assignee_outbound` with a non-None assignment_source raises a serialization error inside apply_async, so the outbound sync task is never enqueued and the assignee change is silently never propagated to the external issue — the opposite of the PR's cross-system sync intent.

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict(self)` (new file `assignment_source.py`), which includes the `queued: datetime` field. That dict is passed into Celery task kwargs as `assignment_source_dict` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` (`sync.py`), via `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={...})`. If the Celery serializer is JSON (a common/default configuration), a raw `datetime` in task kwargs is not JSON-serializable and will fail at enqueue time. The diff shows no conversion (e.g., ISO string) for `queued`, so this is a real defect risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The task signature gains a new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg while `sync_group_assignee_outbound` in sync.py immediately starts sending it unconditionally, so during a rolling deploy old workers running the prior `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` signature receive the extra kwarg and raise TypeError. In mixed-version deployments every queued sync_assignee_outbound task that carries an assignment source fails on old workers with an unexpected-keyword-arg TypeError, losing assignee syncs (and their analytics events) until the deploy completes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task signature `sync_assignee_outbound(...)` to accept a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict` (with a default), and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` now enqueues tasks with `kwargs` that always include the key `assignment_source_dict` (set to `assignment_source.to_dict()` or `None`). In a rolling deploy, any still-running old worker code that has the previous signature `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` would receive an unexpected keyword argument and raise `TypeError`, causing those queued tasks to fail until workers are updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows malformed input by returning None, and the task then calls `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)`, which skips the cycle-prevention check entirely because the `sync_source and ...` guard treats None as 'no source'. A payload that fails to reconstruct (e.g., a `queued` value that becomes a non-datetime after crossing a serialization boundary, or extra keys from a future schema) silently disables cycle prevention for that sync, reintroducing the very sync loops this PR was written to prevent — with no log line recording the drop.

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_assignee_outbound`, `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)` returns `None` on `TypeError`/`ValueError` (e.g., unexpected keys), and then `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` will bypass the cycle-prevention branch because it only runs when `sync_source` is truthy. That’s a real robustness gap: malformed/unexpected task kwargs can silently disable the new cycle-prevention behavior, and there’s no logging when parsing fails. However, the finding’s example about `queued` becoming a non-datetime is not supported by the diff because `cls(**input_dict)` does not enforce types at runtime, so a string `queued` would not necessarily trigger an exception; the bypass mainly occurs with missing required fields or extra/unknown keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cycle-prevention intent is only implemented for assignee sync: `sync_group_assignee_inbound` stamps `assignment_source` on assign/deassign, but `sync_status_inbound` and comment-sync inbound paths were not given the equivalent source tracking, so the stated objective 'prevent sync-cycles' is only partially delivered in this diff. Organizations with two-way status sync enabled still get status ping-pong loops (resolve in Jira -> resolve in Sentry -> re-resolve in Jira), and operators who accepted this PR believing cycle prevention was added will find the assignee-only coverage surprising when the loop they actually hit is a status loop.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a general cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` (issues.py) that blocks syncing when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, but the only diff-shown call site that actually supplies a source is assignee outbound (`sync_assignee_outbound` parses `assignment_source_dict` and calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). Inbound assignee paths stamp `assignment_source` via `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))`. No equivalent source plumbing is shown for status/comment inbound or for the status outbound task call sites (only the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains `assignment_source`, but no wiring is shown). So the finding that cycle prevention is only implemented for assignee sync and not for status/comment paths is grounded in this diff as an incompleteness/scope issue, not a verifiable new defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] sync_group_assignee_outbound puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs via AssignmentSource.to_dict(), which a JSON broker serializes to a string and which old workers (pre-deploy) reject as an unexpected kwarg, causing silent task failure during a rolling deploy. During a rolling deploy, new web nodes enqueue sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source_dict while old workers running the 3-arg signature raise TypeError on the unexpected kwarg; the outbound assignee sync is silently dropped (no retry, no error surfaced), so assignees on external issues fall out of sync. Additionally, after JSON round-trip the 'queued' field is a str, not datetime, so any consumer comparing timestamps gets inconsistent types.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task signature `sync_assignee_outbound` from 3 args to include a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict` (with default), and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` now always enqueues the task with that kwarg in `apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": ...})`. During a rolling deploy, old workers still running the previous 3-arg task implementation would receive an unexpected keyword argument and raise `TypeError`, causing the task to fail. This incompatibility is directly implied by the diff. Additionally, `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` includes `queued` as a raw `datetime` via `asdict(self)`, which may not be safely serializable depending on Celery serializer, and `from_dict` would accept a string for `queued` without validation, leading to inconsistent runtime types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new cycle-prevention test (test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration) has no positive control: it only asserts mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called() and never tests the complementary case where assignment_source.integration_id differs from the target integration, which is the branch the code comment explicitly promises to preserve ('This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward', issues.py:388-390). The assert_not_called assertion cannot distinguish the new sync-cycle gate from any pre-existing early return in should_sync (org_integration None, missing key, config False), and the allow-other-integrations branch of the new gate (sync_source set, integration_id different) ships with zero coverage — a regression that flips it to block all outbound syncs whenever sync_source is present would pass this test suite unchanged.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` to block outbound sync only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, while explicitly intending to still allow other integrations (issues.py:379-391). The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only covers the blocking case (matching integration id) and does not add any test where `assignment_source` is non-None but has a different `integration_id`, i.e. the “allow other integrations” branch. Existing tests cover `assignment_source=None` only. So a regression that incorrectly blocks all outbound sync whenever `sync_source` is present would not be caught by this suite, making the finding a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap (not a proven runtime defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The inbound assignment path — sync_group_assignee_inbound now constructing AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration) and threading it into GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign — is exercised by no assertion anywhere in this diff (I checked tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py and tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py, the only test files touched; neither asserts that an inbound sync passes a non-None assignment_source into assign/deassign). The end-to-end cycle-prevention flow the PR exists for (inbound assign from integration A must not bounce back to A but must propagate to linked integration B) is never verified: if from_integration returns a source whose integration_id never matches (e.g. a type mismatch comparing RpcIntegration.id vs int), cycle prevention silently fails in production while all updated tests still pass, because they only cover the None-source path and the directly-injected source path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in the inbound path: `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` now passes `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` into `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py). Cycle prevention is implemented in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` by checking `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py). The updated/added tests shown only (a) unit-test `AssignmentSource.from_dict/to_dict` and (b) exercise outbound syncing, including an explicit direct injection of `assignment_source` into `GroupAssignee.objects.assign(...)` to ensure outbound doesn’t fire for the same integration. There is no assertion in the shown test changes that an *inbound* call to `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` results in `assign/deassign` receiving a non-None `assignment_source`, nor an end-to-end test that inbound from integration A suppresses outbound back to A. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] test_to_dict's assertion `assert result.get("queued") is not None` is a false-confidence assertion that passes regardless of what queued contains, hiding the import-time-default defect in AssignmentSource itself (assignment_source.py:18: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition time, so every instance shares the module-import timestamp). The test never asserts queued's type or that it approximates the current time, so the stale shared default — which makes every AssignmentSource report the server-start time as its queue time — passes CI while making the field semantically wrong for any consumer using it to measure queue latency or staleness.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `AssignmentSource` as a frozen dataclass with `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (assignment_source.py). In Python, that expression is evaluated once at class definition/import time, so all instances share the same timestamp, which is incorrect for a per-instance “queued” time; it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.
